evidence_requirements.statement: The normal CLI exposes a small stable user surface and keeps schema/versioned subsystem commands compatibility-only.
Public JSON output has stable top-level status and machine-readable contract fields across lifecycle commands.
Explain reports why an action is allowed, blocked, waiting, stale, or escalated, and audit reconstructs intended through landed provenance.
Lifecycle status distinguishes SEALED, LANDABLE or INTEGRATING, and LANDED.
Installation, initialization, upgrade, and migration are deterministic, safe, additive, and preserve historical data and ownership boundaries.
Fresh disposable repositories remain stack-neutral and do not require invented project commands or architecture.
Documentation describes KEEL architecture and public workflow, artifact ownership, upgrades, remote custom-ref replication, and current terminology accurately.
The named control-plane documents and indexes match landed behavior and do not present obsolete lifecycle terminology as the public workflow.
Disposable-repository installation tests demonstrate stack-neutral behavior without invented project commands or architecture.

non_goals: Do not remove historical readers, ledgers, refs, notes, attestations, or migration provenance.
Do not execute remote pushes, merges, releases, deployments, or migrations in consumer repositories.
Do not invent project-language, framework, build, test, or deployment commands for stack-neutral repositories.
Do not manually edit kernel-owned events, grants, receipts, attestations, or generated views.
objective: Refactor KEEL public UX, documentation, packaging, portability, and installation around the redesigned kernel

requirements.statement: The normal CLI converges on init, doctor, start, status, next, run, verify, land, explain, and audit; internal schema/versioned subsystem commands are compatibility-only or hidden from normal help.
Public commands emit stable machine-readable JSON contracts with explicit status and no schema-history-shaped normal interface.
keel explain exposes why an action is allowed, blocked, waiting, stale, or escalated, and keel audit reconstructs intended -> authorized -> executed -> verified -> integrated -> landed provenance.
Public lifecycle status clearly distinguishes SEALED, LANDABLE or INTEGRATING, and LANDED.

Installation is deterministic; ownership classes distinguish KEEL-owned files, project-owned policy/config, generated cache/state, and durable historical ledger data; upgrades and migrations are safe and loss-preserving.
Remote replication guidance documents KEEL custom refs, notes, and attestations where needed.
AGENTS.md remains a short navigational entry point; ARCHITECTURE.md describes KEEL itself; generic target-project policy scaffolding is explicit templates or policy packs.

CONTROL_PLANE.md, WORKFLOW.md, CODEX_NATIVE.md, VERIFICATION.md, ORCHESTRATION.md, and indexes match landed behavior and do not present obsolete Discuss/Plan/Execute/Verify/Ship terminology as the public user workflow.
Fresh installation is tested in representative disposable repositories and KEEL remains stack-neutral without inventing project commands or architecture.

consequences: Changes the public command contract, compatibility boundary, installation behavior, and durable control-plane documentation.
risk.review: Independently review public CLI compatibility, JSON contracts, lifecycle explanations and provenance, safe migration and ownership boundaries, fresh-install portability, remote ref guidance, and documentation consistency.
